The Lisolec is a COMMON-PORT BMS that switches the NEGATIVE leg. B+ is a straight pass-through, so the ROCKER SITS IN THE POSITIVE LEG,

E14 STRADDLES the cut and is the only point the two buses meet — the star ground. E10 now goes straight to the BMS P− pad, not to this board.

E3 — the rocker lamp returns to P−, NOT B−.
E3 — the rocker lamp returns to P−, NOT B−.
So the lamp dies with the load on a BMS trip instead of staying lit off an unprotected node.
So the lamp dies with the load on a BMS trip instead of staying lit off an unprotected node.
E6 — never land 5 V on the LCD until the buck is verified at 5.00 V ±0.1, LOADED.
E6 — never land 5 V on the LCD until the buck is verified at 5.00 V ±0.1, LOADED.
An unverified buck output goes straight into the MCU's VSYS.
An unverified buck output goes straight into the MCU's VSYS.
Gauges — there is NO 14 AWG in the extension.
Gauges — there is NO 14 AWG in the extension.

14 AWG was sized against the old ~6.7 A belief; measured peak is 2.6 A. 18 AWG drops 5.4 mV over 100 mm and fits a perfboard bus, which 14 AWG does not. A JST-XH contact crimps 28–22 AWG, so E8 is 22. The two cell-cap leads stay 16 AWG for thermal mass, not ampacity.

E9 — LiLyGO: SDA = GPIO 17, SCL = GPIO 18 (bench-proven, config.h). Waveshare: SDA 15 / SCL 16.
E9 — LiLyGO: SDA = GPIO 17, SCL = GPIO 18 (bench-proven, config.h). Waveshare: SDA 15 / SCL 16.
On the LiLyGO, GPIO 15 is LCD_Power_On — never land I²C on it there. On the Waveshare, 47/48 are the touch + IMU bus, so the wand gets 15/16. Do not mix the two maps.

USB panel — the two jacks are two GND islands. NEVER bridge them.
USB panel — the two jacks are two GND islands. NEVER bridge them.
Charge-jack GND = BMS P− (via the PD trigger); dev-jack GND = the LCD = P−logic. Joining them parallels E14, the only star point. Meter OPEN before wiring.
Charge-jack GND = BMS P− (via the PD trigger); dev-jack GND = the LCD = P−logic. Joining them parallels E14, the only star point. Meter OPEN before wiring.
E10 — the PD trigger bypasses the rocker by design.
E10 — the PD trigger bypasses the rocker by design.
The pack charges whether the wand is on or off. Dumb CV: the trigger presents 15 V onto the pack via BMS P+/P−, current limited by the PD source, tapering to the BMS's 14.6 V cutoff.

E11 — no 5.1 kΩ CC pull-downs on the panel jacks.
E11 — no 5.1 kΩ CC pull-downs on the panel jacks.
They are passive bulkheads; the PD trigger and the ESP32 each terminate CC themselves. A second sink termination breaks PD negotiation.
